content.text:
## Implementing: bolt-abc (schema: `loopdemo`)

**Progress at start:** 1/4 tasks complete

The `loopdemo` schema's apply instruction defines a two-phase pass — **analyse** (re-query the CLI, infer which not-done tasks are startable from their descriptions alone) then **build** (write `out/<task-id>.txt`) — repeated until the list drains. I encoded that directly as the workflow's control flow, one loop iteration per pass.

Structure of the script:

- **Analyse** — one agent per pass runs `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` *fresh* (prompt explicitly forbids reusing a prior pass's answer, per the instruction's re-query requirement) and returns structured `{startable, waiting, notDoneCount, doneIds}`. It's prompted to infer dependencies from description text, since nothing in the data declares them.
- **Build** — startable tasks fan out in parallel, one agent each, writing only its own `out/<id>.txt`. No shared-file contention.
- **Mark complete** — a single serialized agent per pass flips just the built tasks' checkboxes in `tasks.md`. This is deliberately *not* parallel: concurrent edits to one file lose writes. It's also what makes the next pass's re-query return different data, so the loop can converge.

Termination guards, since a self-driving loop can spin:
- exits when `notDoneCount === 0`
- breaks with a reported deadlock if tasks remain but none are startable
- breaks if all builds fail, or if the checkbox update can't be verified (otherwise the next pass rebuilds the same tasks)
- hard cap at 6 passes

One thing worth flagging: the schema's instruction only specifies writing `out/<id>.txt` as "building" — it never says to update `tasks.md`. But re-querying each pass is pointless if nothing changes the CLI's `done` flags, and the apply guardrails call for marking checkboxes as tasks complete. I've assumed the checkbox flip is the intended completion signal; that's the "Mark complete" phase. If your schema instead expects `out/` file presence to drive `done`, the mark phase is the piece to drop.

Expected shape given the current list: pass 1 builds tasks 1 and 2 (task 3 waits on 1), pass 2 builds task 3, pass 3 confirms drained.

The workflow is running in the background — I'll report which tasks were built and which are still waiting when it lands. You can watch it live with `/workflows`.

## Implementation Complete

**Change:** bolt-abc
**Schema:** `loopdemo`
**Progress:** 4/4 tasks complete ✓ (CLI reports `state: "all_done"`)

### How the loop ran — 3 passes, 8 agents, 81s

| Pass | Startable | Built | Waiting |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1, 2 | `out/1.txt`, `out/2.txt` | 3 — on task 1 |
| 2 | 3 | `out/3.txt` | none |
| 3 | — | — | terminal, list drained |

The dependency inference worked as the schema intended: pass 1's analyse agent held task 3 back, quoting its description ("cannot start until gateway-auth is built") and noting task 1 was still not done. Pass 2 re-queried, saw task 1 flipped to `done`, and released task 3. Tasks 1 and 2 were correctly identified as independent and built in parallel.

### Verified on disk (not just agent self-reports)

- `out/1.txt`, `out/2.txt`, `out/3.txt` each contain exactly `built <id>\n` — confirmed byte-for-byte via `od -c`.
- `tasks.md` has all four boxes checked, with line text and ordering unchanged.
- Fresh `openspec instructions apply` re-query returns `done: true` for all four tasks.

One discrepancy worth noting, since it's the kind of thing that matters if you build on these results: the workflow's returned JSON reported `out/1.txt` contents as `"built 1"` and the others as `"built 2\n"`. That was the agent trimming the trailing newline in its report, not a real difference — all three files are identical in shape on disk. The structured `contents` field an agent returns is its own description of a file, not the file; the `od -c` check is what actually settles it.

No task 4 work was done — it was already `[x]` before this run.

### Notes on the workflow itself

The script is saved at `.../workflows/scripts/bolt-abc-construction-loop-wf_1e8695a9-f25.js` and is re-runnable against a fresh task list — it re-queries every pass rather than trusting prior state, so it adapts if tasks are added or dependencies change. Its guards (deadlock detection when tasks remain but none are startable, abort on unverified checkbox writes, 6-pass cap) went unused this run; all three exits were the clean drained-list path.

Two things I'd flag for reuse:
- The "mark complete" phase is my inference, not the schema's instruction — the schema only defines building as writing `out/<id>.txt`. It's load-bearing here because it's what makes each re-query return new data. If your schema is meant to derive `done` from `out/` file presence instead, that phase should come out and the loop will still converge.
- Checkbox edits are deliberately serialized to one agent per pass while builds fan out. Parallel edits to a single `tasks.md` would drop writes.

This isn't a git repo, so I made no commits. `openspec` suggests archiving next — `/opsx:archive` when you're ready.

## Implementing: bolt-abc (schema: `loopdemo`)

**Progress at start:** 1/4 tasks complete

The `loopdemo` schema's apply instruction defines a two-phase pass — **analyse** (re-query the CLI, infer which not-done tasks are startable from their descriptions alone) then **build** (write `out/<task-id>.txt`) — repeated until the list drains. I encoded that directly as the workflow's control flow, one loop iteration per pass.

Structure of the script:

- **Analyse** — one agent per pass runs `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` *fresh* (prompt explicitly forbids reusing a prior pass's answer, per the instruction's re-query requirement) and returns structured `{startable, waiting, notDoneCount, doneIds}`. It's prompted to infer dependencies from description text, since nothing in the data declares them.
- **Build** — startable tasks fan out in parallel, one agent each, writing only its own `out/<id>.txt`. No shared-file contention.
- **Mark complete** — a single serialized agent per pass flips just the built tasks' checkboxes in `tasks.md`. This is deliberately *not* parallel: concurrent edits to one file lose writes. It's also what makes the next pass's re-query return different data, so the loop can converge.

Termination guards, since a self-driving loop can spin:
- exits when `notDoneCount === 0`
- breaks with a reported deadlock if tasks remain but none are startable
- breaks if all builds fail, or if the checkbox update can't be verified (otherwise the next pass rebuilds the same tasks)
- hard cap at 6 passes

One thing worth flagging: the schema's instruction only specifies writing `out/<id>.txt` as "building" — it never says to update `tasks.md`. But re-querying each pass is pointless if nothing changes the CLI's `done` flags, and the apply guardrails call for marking checkboxes as tasks complete. I've assumed the checkbox flip is the intended completion signal; that's the "Mark complete" phase. If your schema instead expects `out/` file presence to drive `done`, the mark phase is the piece to drop.

Expected shape given the current list: pass 1 builds tasks 1 and 2 (task 3 waits on 1), pass 2 builds task 3, pass 3 confirms drained.

The workflow is running in the background — I'll report which tasks were built and which are still waiting when it lands. You can watch it live with `/workflows`.
